meaning.en: To have a relaxed chat about everyday matters, family and daily life.
meaning.zh: 随意聊聊日常生活和家里的事。

examples.zh: 奶奶搬个小凳子，坐在门口跟邻居拉家常。
examples.en: Grandma pulled up a stool and chatted with the neighbours at the door.

examples.zh: 领导下乡调研，先和村民拉了拉家常。
examples.en: The official visiting the village first chatted casually with the villagers.

usage.en: Warm and informal; officials '拉家常' to put people at ease. Splits: 拉拉家常.
usage.zh: 亲切随和，干部下乡常用来拉近距离。可重叠为“拉拉家常”。

natural: a person down on their luck

meaning.en: A villain or loser who has fallen from power and is at others' mercy.
meaning.zh: 比喻失势的坏人。

examples.zh: 他现在是落水狗，谁都想踩一脚。
examples.en: He's down and out now, and everyone wants to kick him.

examples.zh: 对落水狗不能心软，否则后患无穷。
examples.en: Don't go soft on a fallen enemy, or you'll regret it.

usage.en: Derogatory. Famous from Lu Xun's 'Fair play should be put off' (论“费厄泼赖”应该缓行): 痛打落水狗, beat the dog in the water.
usage.zh: 含贬义。鲁迅有“痛打落水狗”之说。

meaning.en: A person with only half-baked skill or knowledge who does things unreliably.
meaning.zh: 指知识技能不到家、做事不踏实的人。

examples.zh: 他是个半吊子，别指望他能修好电脑。
examples.en: He's a dabbler; don't expect him to fix the computer.

examples.zh: 学了三天就教人，真是半吊子。
examples.en: Teaching after three days of learning is just half-baked.

usage.en: Derogatory, can be self-mocking. Also an adjective: 半吊子工程 (shoddy project).
usage.zh: 含贬义，也可自嘲。可作定语。

meaning.en: To lie in ambush; figuratively, to hold back one's real strength or hide something.
meaning.zh: 本指设伏兵；比喻隐藏实力或把东西藏起来。

examples.zh: 他开会总打埋伏，从不提前亮出底牌。
examples.en: He always holds back at meetings and never shows his hand early.

examples.zh: 公司账上有一笔钱被他打了埋伏。
examples.en: He tucked away a sum of money in the company's accounts.

usage.en: Military origin (ambush); figuratively used for hiding things or effort.
usage.zh: 本为军事用语，后比喻藏着掖着。

meaning.en: To take the leading role in a play or an activity.
meaning.zh: 担任主要角色；在某件事中起主导作用。

examples.zh: 这次谈判由经济部门唱主角。
examples.en: The economic department takes the lead in these negotiations.

examples.zh: 年轻人如今已成为消费市场上唱主角的人群。
examples.en: Young people are now the main players in the consumer market.

usage.en: From opera. Opposite: 唱配角.
usage.zh: 源自戏曲，反义“唱配角”。

meaning.en: To show off one's power or authority in an overbearing way.
meaning.zh: 炫耀权势，摆出威严的样子。

examples.zh: 他刚当上组长就在大家面前耍威风。
examples.en: He started lording it over everyone as soon as he became team leader.

examples.zh: 别在我面前耍威风，我不吃这一套。
examples.en: Don't throw your weight around with me; it won't work.

usage.en: Derogatory.
usage.zh: 含贬义。

meaning.en: Someone who can do a bit of everything but is expert in nothing; also something said to work for anything.
meaning.zh: 指什么都会一点但都不精的人，或指什么场合都能用的东西。

examples.zh: 他在公司是万金油，哪个部门缺人就去哪个。
examples.en: He's the company's all-rounder, sent wherever a department is short.

examples.zh: “多喝热水”被调侃成治百病的万金油。
examples.en: 'Drink more hot water' is joked about as the cure-all for everything.

usage.en: From Tiger Balm (万金油), an ointment sold as a cure for many ailments. Can be praise or mockery.
usage.zh: 来自万金油这种什么病都抹的药膏，可褒可贬。

natural: laugh it off; joke to dodge

meaning.en: To joke or laugh to avoid a serious subject; to make light of something.
meaning.zh: 开玩笑；用说笑的方式敷衍过去。

examples.zh: 问他什么时候还钱，他只是打哈哈。
examples.en: Asked when he'd pay back the money, he just laughed it off.

examples.zh: 别跟我打哈哈，说正经的。
examples.en: Don't joke your way out of this; be serious.

usage.en: Two senses: joking around, and dodging a question.
usage.zh: 有说笑和敷衍两种意思。

meaning.en: To weigh up costs and benefits, often for selfish ends.
meaning.zh: 盘算得失，多指为自己精打细算。

examples.zh: 他心里早就打好了算盘，不会吃亏的。
examples.en: He's already worked out the sums and won't lose out.

examples.zh: 你别打错算盘，这事没那么容易。
examples.en: Don't miscalculate; this isn't as easy as you think.

usage.en: Often 如意算盘 (wishful calculation) or 打错算盘 (miscalculate). Literally clicking abacus beads.
usage.zh: 常说“如意算盘”“打错算盘”。

meaning.en: To get money or gifts from others, using a relationship or a pretext.
meaning.zh: 借故向人索取财物。

examples.zh: 远房亲戚又来家里打秋风了。
examples.en: The distant relatives have come to scrounge again.

examples.zh: 他一年到头到处打秋风，从不自己挣钱。
examples.en: He scrounges everywhere all year and never earns a thing.

usage.en: Derogatory. Also written 打抽丰. The 'autumn wind' relates to harvest-time visits; the exact origin is debated.
usage.zh: 含贬义。也写作“打抽丰”。来源有争议。

meaning.en: To show off one's status or make unreasonable demands to seem important.
meaning.zh: 故意显示排场和身份，摆出架势。

examples.zh: 她刚红起来就开始摆谱，出门要带五个助理。
examples.en: She started putting on airs once she got famous, taking five assistants everywhere.

examples.zh: 他请客时爱摆谱，专点最贵的菜。
examples.en: He likes to show off when hosting, ordering the priciest dishes.

usage.en: Northern colloquial; can be written 摆谱儿. Opposite of 低调.
usage.zh: 北方口语，常儿化为“摆谱儿”。反义“低调”。

meaning.en: A person who looks friendly but is cunning and ruthless underneath.
meaning.zh: 外表和善、内心阴险狠毒的人。

examples.zh: 别被他的笑脸骗了，他是个笑面虎。
examples.en: Don't be fooled by his smile; he's a smiling tiger.

examples.zh: 这个笑面虎，一边夸你一边在背后捅刀。
examples.en: That smiling villain praises you while stabbing you in the back.

usage.en: Derogatory. Compare 口蜜腹剑.
usage.zh: 含贬义。可对照“口蜜腹剑”。

meaning.en: A sharp, painful drop after a period of growth, especially in an economy.
meaning.zh: 比喻经济等在高速发展后急剧下滑。

examples.zh: 专家担心经济会出现硬着陆。
examples.en: Experts fear the economy will have a hard landing.

examples.zh: 政策调整得当，市场避免了硬着陆。
examples.en: With proper policy adjustment, the market avoided a hard landing.

usage.en: Borrowed from aviation and economics. Its counterpart is the soft landing (软着陆). 着 is zhuó here.
usage.zh: 借自航空和经济学术语，对应的说法是“软着陆”。“着”读zhuó。

meaning.en: To misjudge something by looking, e.g. take a fake for real.
meaning.zh: 看错了；因判断失误而看走了眼。

examples.zh: 这回我走眼了，没想到他这么能干。
examples.en: I misjudged him; I never thought he'd be so capable.

examples.zh: 古董商也有走眼的时候。
examples.en: Even antique dealers get it wrong at times.

usage.en: Often 看走眼 or 走了眼. Slight self-reproach.
usage.zh: 常说“看走眼”“走了眼”。

natural: treat oneself to a good meal

meaning.en: To have a good meal with meat as a treat, after plain fare.
meaning.zh: 平时吃得简单，偶尔改善伙食，吃一顿好的。

examples.zh: 周末我们去火锅店打打牙祭。
examples.en: This weekend let's treat ourselves at the hotpot place.

examples.zh: 发了工资，他请大家打牙祭。
examples.en: On payday he treated everyone to a good meal.

usage.en: Sichuan origin: 牙祭 was a meat offering on the 1st and 15th. Casual.
usage.zh: 源自四川，旧时逢初一十五用肉祭神，后称吃肉改善伙食。

natural: be left in an awkward spot

meaning.en: To be put in an embarrassing position with no graceful way out.
meaning.zh: 处境尴尬，没法体面收场。

examples.zh: 当众被问倒了，他一时下不来台。
examples.en: Stumped in public, he was left without a graceful way out.

examples.zh: 你这样说，会让他下不来台的。
examples.en: Saying that, how is he supposed to save face?

usage.en: Often with 让/使 (cause someone). Positive counterpart: 给台阶下.
usage.zh: 常与“让”连用；反义“给台阶下”。

meaning.en: To live as an unmarried man.
meaning.zh: 男子没有结婚，单身过日子。

examples.zh: 他三十五岁了还在打光棍。
examples.en: He's thirty-five and still a bachelor.

examples.zh: 村里有不少打光棍的小伙子。
examples.en: The village has quite a few young men who have no wives.

usage.en: Used of men; teasing or sympathetic. 光棍节 (Singles' Day, 11.11) is related.
usage.zh: 指男性，调侃或同情。光棍节与此相关。

natural: act as a go-between for vice

meaning.en: To procure for prostitution; figuratively, to broker shady deals.
meaning.zh: 本指为嫖客和妓女牵线；比喻为不正当交易牵线搭桥。

examples.zh: 他靠给官员拉皮条赚了不少钱。
examples.en: He made plenty by brokering shady deals for officials.

examples.zh: 别给我拉皮条，我不干这种事。
examples.en: Don't try to act as a go-between for me; I don't do that.

usage.en: Vulgar and derogatory. Use with care.
usage.zh: 粗俗，含强烈贬义，慎用。

natural: strike it rich by luck or foul means

meaning.en: To make a fortune suddenly through luck or improper means.
meaning.zh: 靠意外机会或不正当手段突然发财。

examples.zh: 他整天想着发横财，却不愿踏实干活。
examples.en: He dreams of getting rich quick but won't work steadily.

examples.zh: 听说那家人靠拆迁发了横财。
examples.en: They say that family made a fortune from the demolition compensation.

usage.en: 横 is hèng (unexpected, improper). Often critical of get-rich-quick thinking.
usage.zh: “横”读hèng，指意外、不正当。多批评一夜暴富的想法。

meaning.en: A jumble of different things thrown together; originally a mixed stew.
meaning.zh: 把各种东西混杂在一起；本指什么菜都放进去的一锅菜。

examples.zh: 这本书是各种资料拼成的大杂烩。
examples.en: The book is a hotchpotch of various sources.

examples.zh: 今晚的菜是一锅大杂烩，味道还不错。
examples.en: Tonight's dish is a big mixed stew, and tastes decent.

usage.en: Both literal (a dish) and figurative; the figurative sense is often critical.
usage.zh: 既指菜肴，也比喻杂乱，后者常带批评。

meaning.en: Plain, simple spoken language that anyone can understand.
meaning.zh: 通俗易懂的口头语言。

examples.zh: 请用大白话给我解释一下这个术语。
examples.en: Please explain this term to me in plain language.

examples.zh: 这篇文章全是大白话，一看就懂。
examples.en: The article is all plain language and easy to follow.

usage.en: Neutral to positive; often a request: 说大白话.
usage.zh: 中性偏褒，常说“用大白话讲”。

meaning.en: A small gift, or a task that is easy and not worth mentioning.
meaning.zh: 一点小心意；或指轻而易举的小事。

examples.zh: 这是一点小意思，请您收下。
examples.en: This is a small token; please accept it.

examples.zh: 修个水龙头，小意思！
examples.en: Fixing a tap? A piece of cake!

usage.en: Two uses: gift-giving modesty and breezy confidence. 意思 is yì si in neutral tone.
usage.zh: 既用于送礼谦辞，也用于表示事情轻而易举。“意思”读yì si。

meaning.en: To play the kind, conciliatory role while someone else plays the stern one.
meaning.zh: 在人面前扮演和善、宽容的角色。

examples.zh: 你来唱红脸，我来唱白脸，一起把孩子教好。
examples.en: You play the good cop and I'll play the bad cop, so we raise the child well.

examples.zh: 他总是红脸，从不批评员工。
examples.en: He always plays the nice guy and never criticises staff.

usage.en: From opera face-painting: red = loyal and upright, white = treacherous. Pairs with 唱白脸.
usage.zh: 源自戏曲脸谱：红脸忠厚，白脸奸诈。常与“唱白脸”对举。

meaning.en: To talk in lofty, impressive terms but not act on them.
meaning.zh: 说得很漂亮，却不切实际、不去做。

examples.zh: 少唱高调，先把眼前的事做好。
examples.en: Stop talking big and get the task in front of you done.

examples.zh: 他在台上唱高调，私下里却是另一套。
examples.en: He preaches high ideals on stage and does otherwise in private.

usage.en: Derogatory. Opposite 低调 (low profile).
usage.zh: 含贬义，反义“低调”。

meaning.en: A comment or action that comes too late to help; speaking wisely only after the event.
meaning.zh: 事后才发表意见或采取行动，为时已晚。

examples.zh: 事情都过去了，你现在说这些简直是马后炮。
examples.en: It's all over; saying this now is just hindsight.

examples.zh: 他总爱放马后炮，出事前一句话也不说。
examples.en: He loves to be wise after the event and says nothing before things go wrong.

usage.en: Said to come from xiangqi (Chinese chess), where a cannon behind the horse is a late attack. Derogatory.
usage.zh: 一说出自象棋，“马后炮”是将军的一招；此处比喻为时已晚。含贬义。
